answer: Because the relic salt is published after the timber checkpoint, the vertex audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 211 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. An operator running 32 keys thus pays for 32 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
